decisions.question: G11 against Spec §10.2 principle 5 and ADR-003 item 2 as amended: where does the statement that a subscriber's exception never reaches the scheduler live, and which case checks it, given that nidana.runtime.5 to .12 replay bus-testing with --guarantee G5,G6,G7,G8,G10,G11 before any publisher, observed stream, start() or TestBus.input exists?

options.label: S58's sentence appended to G11, checked by the first G3 case
options.consequence: G11 keeps its id and its scheduler meaning and gains the subscriber sentence; the check needs a delivering bus, so it sits in the G3 case, which v1 already used to check where a TestBus's subscriber errors go and which nidana.runtime.13 delivers; the gates of .5 to .12 select the same G11 case as before; Validation names the case that checks G11's sentence.

options.label: A new guarantee G21 for subscriber errors on a virtual provider
options.consequence: Clean one-to-one mapping of sentence to case, but a new id that every restricted gate must add (H11), and G11, the guarantee the intake names, would only point at it.

options.label: A new G11 case
options.consequence: The case needs observe, a publisher, start() and TestBus.input; every gate from nidana.runtime.5 to .12 selects G11 and would fail on UnimplementedError until .13.

decisions.chosen: S58's sentence appended to G11, checked by the first G3 case
decisions.why: The meaning of G11 carries over and the Delivery paragraph already puts G3 at nidana.runtime.13, where TestBus.input lands; v1's G3 case was where a TestBus subscriber's error zone was checked, so the check stays where the gates expect it. The case also runs the throwing delivery inside triggerActions() (a reentrant drain), which bus-api@v2's own G18 cases do not, so it checks 'never reaches the scheduler' and not only 'reaches the listen zone'. Signal that would have changed my mind: H11 moving publishers and observed streams before nidana.runtime.5, which would let a G11 case run there.

decisions.question: G4: keep its meaning as measured, or take S58's optional strengthening (the timers and microtasks a subscriber's callbacks create run only inside a scheduler operation, wherever the test listens from)?

options.label: Adopt the strengthening, limited to a subscriber's own callbacks
options.consequence: G4 names callbacks passed to listen on an observed stream or set later through the subscription, and leaves out operators chained onto the stream (RxDart creates some of their timers at listen, ADR-003 Consequences); a new case pins it; a runtime that binds callbacks to the listen zone, which ADR-003 rejected, fails it.

options.label: Keep G4 as written
options.consequence: The fact still follows from bus-api@v2 G5 and this contract's G6, but nothing in bus-testing's suite would catch a runtime that satisfies Spec §10.2 by binding callbacks to the listen zone and loses virtual time for them.

decisions.chosen: Adopt the strengthening, limited to a subscriber's own callbacks
decisions.why: ADR-003 item 2 chose forwarding over binding precisely because binding makes a callback's timers real on a TestBus (subscriber-error-zone C7, C8, T3, T4); pinning it in the test substrate makes that reason executable. Compatible: the new case passes on the bus-api@v1 stand-in and the binding defect fails it.
evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/bus-testing-v0151/output.txt T4, T7 (defect: callbacks bound to the zone that listened)

decisions.question: Seven v1 cases activate a MODULE topology before start(), which bus-api@v2 G42 rejects. How is each rewritten, and does its meaning change?

options.label: APPLICATION before start() for six, MODULE after start() for the G18 isolation case
options.consequence: 'G4 a bus on a virtual provider...' (debounced), 'G12 settle delivers...' (doubler), 'G13 a TestBus numbers...' (doubler), 'G13 two TestBuses...' (debounced), 'G18 stub rejects...' (owner, which keeps pinning that a stub's claim is checked at once during bootstrap) and 'G19 an ordering probe reports one sequence...' (echo) activate an APPLICATION topology before start(); 'G18 a test activates only the topologies under test...' (derive) stubs, starts, then activates its MODULE topology, the pattern 'How a test uses it' now prescribes. None of the seven changes meaning.

options.label: APPLICATION before start() for all seven
options.consequence: Smallest diff, but no case would exercise the MODULE-after-start() isolation pattern consumers must now follow.

options.label: Start first for all seven
options.consequence: Nothing would pin that a stub's claim is rejected at once during bootstrap (Spec §3.13 'validate and claim at once').

decisions.chosen: APPLICATION before start() for six, MODULE after start() for the G18 isolation case
decisions.why: Same rule as S60: keep a bootstrap check where the case is about one, start first where the case is about the post-start pattern. Each rewritten case passes on both the bus-api@v1 and the bus-api@v2 stand-in, so none pins a change.

decisions.question: G3 and G11: what of a timer or microtask that a subscriber's callback creates and that then throws? Its callback runs in the provider zone (bus-api@v2 G5), so the timer is scheduled work there, and its error goes to the zone that built the scheduler, not the zone that listened.

options.label: State it in G11 and pin it in the G3 case
options.consequence: The G3 case's throwing timer is created inside the subscriber's callback; the case expects the callback's own exception in the listen zone and the timer's in the construction zone; a binding runtime fails it too.

options.label: Leave it implied by bus-api@v2 G5 and G11's general rule
options.consequence: A reader of G11 could take every error that starts in a subscriber to go to the listen zone.

decisions.chosen: State it in G11 and pin it in the G3 case
decisions.why: It is the one place where the amended zone rule and the scheduler's rule meet, and a test author would otherwise guess wrong. It follows from ADR-003 items 2 and 5 and needs no new behavior; the v2 stand-in shows it (T4).

decisions.question: G14 for a recorder attached during bootstrap, which Spec §3.13 and bus-api@v2 G34 now deliver to at start(): restate and pin, or leave G14 as is because the recorder rule (each delivery, in delivery order) is unchanged?

options.label: Restate G14 and add a bootstrap case
options.consequence: G14 says a recorder attached during bootstrap, TestBus.recorder included, records nothing before start() and then the publishes the bootstrap connections cause, in the connection order, an event no later-connected reader receives included, then the queue; the case records ['testing.derived:2', 'testing.out:4', 'testing.e:7'] on the v2 stand-in and ['testing.e:7', 'testing.out:0', 'testing.derived:2'] on the v1 stand-in.

options.label: Leave G14's text
options.consequence: True as a rule, but a consumer reading it would not learn that TestBus.recorder's contents for a bootstrap script changed, and nothing in this suite would catch a recorder that skips start()'s connection deliveries.

decisions.chosen: Restate G14 and add a bootstrap case
decisions.why: The intake names G14 for exactly this; the replay shows the recorded contents and order change for the same script, which is what consumers assert on. The seeded defect that skips recorders during start()'s connection step fails only this case.

decisions.question: G19 for an OrderingProbe attached during bootstrap: its first values were 'what bus-api@v1 G17 delivers first' (a microtask after listen, even during bootstrap); restate for bus-api@v2 G17 and G34?

options.label: Restate G19 with both cases and add a bootstrap case
options.consequence: After start(): the current value or buffer, in the first provider-zone microtask after listen (G17); during bootstrap: nothing before start(), then the value start() settled, within start() (G34); the case expects [[], [], []] before start(), [[2], [2], [2]] after it and [[2, 10], ...] after triggerActions; the v1 stand-in gives [[0], [0], [0]] before start().

options.label: Only move the citation to bus-api@v2 G17
options.consequence: G17 of v2 covers only subscriptions made after start(), so G19 would say nothing of a bootstrap probe.

decisions.chosen: Restate G19 with both cases and add a bootstrap case
decisions.why: Named by the intake; v2 G17 no longer covers bootstrap, so a citation move alone would leave a gap. Two seeded defects (connection publishes deferred to a microtask, subscriptions connected before topologies) fail the new case.

decisions.question: 'How a test uses it' (OQ-R2's isolation answer) against Spec §7.2's scope timing: v1 had a VM test activate the topologies under test before start() and a widget test attach a recorder before start(), with no word on when a page or module scope mounts.

options.label: Restate both bullets for scope timing and connection at start()
options.consequence: VM test: APPLICATION topologies before start(), which connects them writers first and delivers their connections' publishes before the queued inputs; MODULE and PAGE topologies after start(), with event inputs published after activation; a subscriber's timers are virtual and its exception fails the test that listened. Widget test: start() before pumping a tree that mounts a page or module scope, as an app calls start() before its UI mounts.

options.label: Cite bus-api@v2 G42 and leave the bullets
options.consequence: The documented usage would still tell consumers to do what now throws.

decisions.chosen: Restate both bullets for scope timing and connection at start()
decisions.why: The usage section is normative guidance consumers build against; leaving it would document a pattern bus-api@v2 rejects. The widget bullet states only what G42 forces; flutter-binding's helpers stay H6's.

decisions.question: G18: state that input and stub work during bootstrap, a stub's claim checked at once (bus-api@v2 G34, G42)?

options.label: Add one sentence
options.consequence: Makes explicit that scope timing does not touch the test's publishers (G42 exempts publishers of any scope); compatible, since v1's G18 cases already stub before start() and pass on both stand-ins.

options.label: Leave G18's text
options.consequence: A reader of the new scope-timing bullet might wonder whether stub before start() is still allowed.

decisions.why: Cheap clarification with no behavior change; no evidence needed beyond the passing v1 cases.

decisions.question: Classify every change against this contract's Breaking list (DEC-688): does bus-testing take v2, or stay within v1 because every behavioral change is bus-api@v2's, which already versioned it?

options.label: v2: the recorder's and the probe's bootstrap contents, the TestBus's error zone and its scope timing are breaking; G4 and the citations compatible
options.consequence: bus-testing.md becomes v2 with one migration entry per change; every live citation of bus-testing@v1 elsewhere (155 citations in 24 files, listed in notes) moves to @v2 inside the intake, through the same touches that move bus-api's; consumers are all bus-api consumers already re-confirming for bus-api@v2.

options.label: Compatible within v1, as a dated amendment
options.consequence: No citation churn; but v1's suite fails 8 of 47 on a bus-api@v2 runtime, which the Compatible list's 'a new guarantee that existing fixtures still pass' excludes, TestBus.recorder records other contents in another order for a bootstrap script (the list names 'what a recorder records or in which order'), and the usage v1 documented throws.

decisions.chosen: v2: the recorder's and the probe's bootstrap contents, the TestBus's error zone and its scope timing are breaking; G4 and the citations compatible
decisions.why: Replay: the v2 suite fails exactly three cases on the bus-api@v1 stand-in (the G3 error-zone case, the G14 and G19 bootstrap cases) and passes 50 of 50 on the v2 stand-in; v1's suite fails 8 of 47 on the v2 stand-in. The G14 change is literally on the Breaking list; the others fail existing fixtures, which the Compatible list does not allow. Each breaking change is the Specification's, reached through bus-api@v2 and ADR-003 as amended, so the choice was the version number, not the behavior. Signal that would have changed my mind: an orchestrator reading of DEC-688 under which a contract that incorporates another by reference (G3's last sentence) versions only for its own rules.

decisions.question: Should v2's Breaking list name what this step had to argue from the Compatible list: what an ordering probe receives, and moving G3 to a breaking version of bus-api?

options.label: Add both items
options.consequence: A later classification is literal: a breaking bus-api version reached through G3 versions bus-testing, and a probe's received sequence is part of the contract.

options.label: Keep v1's list
options.consequence: The next intake re-argues the same question from the Compatible list.

decisions.why: Removes the ambiguity this step met; changes nothing for consumers today. No evidence beyond this step's own classification.
